meta.title: Android Runtime (ART), DEX, OAT & Execution Engine
meta.subtitle: Beginner → Expert Masterclass Roadmap
meta.completionMessage: Congratulations! You have completed the masterclass roadmap for ART, DEX, OAT, and the Android execution engine—covering everything from virtual machine internals and bytecode verification to JIT/AOT compilation, garbage collection, and reverse engineering!

details.title: Execution Pipeline
items: Java/Kotlin Source → Java/Kotlin Compiler → DEX Bytecode → ART Runtime → ARM64 Native Machine Code → CPU Execution

items: System boot → Zygote process starts ART → Boot image loaded → Core libraries initialized → Class preloading (preloaded-classes) → GC initialization → Thread initialization → Ready for application forks

details.title: Application Launch Pipeline
items: Launcher → ActivityManagerService → Zygote Socket → fork() → Pre-initialized ART runtime inherited → Application class instantiation → ClassLoader setup → ActivityThread → Application.onCreate() → First Activity launch

details.title: Runtime Execution Inquiry
items: Is this method running under interpreter, JIT native code, or AOT compiled code?
Which ClassLoader loaded this class (PathClassLoader vs Custom DexClassLoader)?
Has the target method been inlined by the Optimizing Compiler?
Is the call site using virtual dispatch (vtable) or direct dispatch?
Does execution cross into native space via JNI?
Is the object residing in Zygote space, Boot Image, or Application Heap?
Has Profile-Guided Optimization altered execution paths?
Why might static decompilation differ from runtime behavior due to compiler optimizations?
